Phase 1 RCA — CONFIRMED DEFECT.

Mechanism: the deterministic `plan_review_assemble_criteria` step can raise `CriteriaError` while loading the repository criteria overlay (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:197-252`). The workflow interpreter records every scripted exception only as a string (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py:419-511`). After coach/verify recovery, `produce_plan_review_verdict` treats every remaining failed workflow as an LLM-finder failure (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:235-243`) and passes it to `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`, which unconditionally stamps `coverage.llm_unavailable=True` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:303-340`). That source-blind tail is the direct root cause; exception identity loss is contributing, not sufficient.

Discriminating runtime proof on current origin/main c6f20ceb0b: an ephemeral full-gate probe injected `CriteriaError("phase1 malformed-overlay sentinel")` from `registry.effective_criteria`. The recorder showed failed frame `review@then/assemble`, kind `scripted`, and zero executed agent/batch frames, yet the public verdict was INDETERMINATE with full DET coverage, `llm_ran=False`, and `llm_unavailable=True`. A genuine preflight `LLMUnavailableError` control remained unavailable; a healthy FakeRunner control returned PASS with `llm_ran=True` and no unavailable flag. Injecting a typed `CriteriaError` directly as `RunResult.error` still produced `llm_unavailable=True`, proving the broad tail itself is sufficient. A same-frame identity differential showed CriteriaError, RuntimeError, and LLMUnavailableError all emerge from the generic interpreter as identical strings, confirming the enabling information loss. The ephemeral probe was deleted; the worktree is clean.

Legitimacy: DEFECT. Original epic jira-reb-687 explicitly replaces the opaque single-error collapse and scopes the unavailable/disposition behavior to LLM failures. `docs/config.md:335-365`, ADR 0040, and gate_dispatch’s own module contract likewise describe only LLM call/tier failures as `llm_unavailable`. A local criteria/config parse failure is not an LLM failure.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is fail-closed INDETERMINATE with DET coverage and a distinct installed-build/config-fault diagnostic; genuine preflight and mid-run LLM outages remain unchanged. `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` has only those two genuine outage callers plus the generic failed tail. Splitting only a structured CriteriaError marker from the tail finds no caller relying on the mislabel.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report

Problem
A malformed or stale project criteria configuration caused plan review to return an unsigned INDETERMINATE result labeled as llm_unavailable, even though no provider call ran. This sent operators toward provider credentials instead of the installed-build/configuration mismatch.

Proven root cause
The assemble-criteria scripted step raised CriteriaError, but the generic workflow recorder preserved only an undifferentiated failed-step string. Gate dispatch therefore reached the source-blind degraded tail, which classified every unrecognized tail failure as an LLM outage. The loss of typed failure identity at the recorder boundary was the causal defect.

Experiments
A held-out end-to-end workflow test injected a sentinel CriteriaError at criteria assembly. Before the fix it reproduced the false llm_unavailable classification. The fix made it GREEN. Removing the structured dispatch route made the same test RED again, and restoring the route returned it to GREEN. The test also proves that non-CriteriaError failures retain generic LLM degradation behavior and that deterministic blockers/coverage survive the local config fault.

Fix
Criteria assembly now emits a failed StepResult with stable failure_kind=criteria_config and the original diagnostic. Verdict dispatch recognizes only that exact failed assemble frame and marker before generic degradation, reruns the deterministic floor, preserves deterministic findings, reports config_fault without llm_unavailable, and gives actionable repository-checkout/installed-build remediation. The output schema documents the new structured fields.

Held-out disclosure
The original held-out source had been deleted and no byte-identical copy was available. The regression was reconstructed from the frozen behavioral contract before production edits; this limitation is disclosed rather than claiming source identity.

Validation
RED to GREEN to mutation RED to restored GREEN; 235 passed and 8 skipped in the focused validation; lint, typecheck, diff check, DCO, commit-ticket verification, and independent cross-review all passed. Gerrit change 1568 earned LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, zero unresolved comments, and merged on 2026-08-09.

Per operator directive, this ticket remains in_progress and is not closed.

# A stale installed build must fail loudly, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

## Context
A stale installed rebar build rejected the repository's dict-shaped `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` with `CriteriaError`, but plan review emitted an ordinary unsigned INDETERMINATE carrying `llm_ran: false` and `llm_unavailable: true`. The DET tier still appeared, so a broken install looked like a ticket that could not be reviewed. Predecessor `inexistent-tempting-nerka` repaired the machine-local updater; this ticket is the durable repository repair. Control flow must remain fail-closed and continue emitting a verdict.

## Confirmed root cause and authority
The deterministic assemble step loads effective criteria. The generic workflow interpreter stringifies its exception, then `produce_plan_review_verdict` routes every unrecovered workflow failure through the systemic-LLM degraded builder. That builder hardcodes `llm_unavailable: true`, even when the recorded failed frame is the scripted assemble step and no LLM/batch frame executed. Runtime differential proof and exact citations are recorded in the Phase 1 RCA comment.

This is a defect against original epic jira-reb-687, which explicitly replaced opaque LLM error collapse and scoped unavailable/disposition behavior to LLM failures. `docs/config.md` and ADR 0040 preserve the same boundary. Criteria configuration parsing is not an LLM call.

## Repair plan
- At the criteria-assembly boundary, catch the exact shared criteria exception and return a failed workflow step with a stable structured failure kind plus the original diagnostic. Do not classify by matching error-message text.
- Before the generic failed-tail LLM degradation, inspect the recorded failed assemble step. Route only the structured criteria/config failure kind to a dedicated plan-review config-fault verdict path. Genuine preflight and mid-run `LLMUnavailableError` paths remain byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.
- Build the config-fault verdict from the same deterministic floor and partitioning path, preserving DET findings. Its coverage must mark a distinct config fault, omit the affirmative `llm_unavailable` label, and contain an actionable diagnostic that names the running installed rebar build as the suspect and points the operator to the repository checkout build.
- Teach terminal verdict assembly that a systemic config fault is INDETERMINATE unless an actionable deterministic blocker already makes it BLOCK. This preserves fail-closed behavior without reusing the LLM-outage flag.
- Document the structured failure marker in the assemble-step output contract.
- Add focused regression coverage through the public verdict seam, paired with genuine LLM-outage and healthy controls.

## Testing
The held-out oracle will drive the real workflow gate with a successful fake provider while injecting the exact shared criteria exception at effective-criteria assembly. It will prove the fixture reached the scripted assemble frame before any agent/batch work, assert the observable verdict/coverage contract, and compare against a genuine provider outage. The existing gate-cutover and LLM failure-matrix tests remain controls. Canonical lint, typecheck, focused tests, and the relevant workflow/plan-review suite must pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Injecting the shared `CriteriaError` during real criteria assembly yields an unsigned fail-closed verdict with `verdict: INDETERMINATE`, `llm_ran: false`, full DET coverage, a distinct config-fault field, and no affirmative `llm_unavailable` field.
- [ ] The config-fault diagnostic explicitly names the running INSTALLED REBAR BUILD as the suspect and directs the reader to use the repository checkout build; it preserves the original parse diagnostic without using string matching to classify it.
- [ ] A negative-control genuine `LLMUnavailableError` still produces `llm_unavailable: true`; a healthy fake-provider control still runs the LLM tier and never reports a config fault.
- [ ] The structured failure kind is carried from the exact criteria exception at the assemble boundary and documented in that step's output contract. Other assemble/runtime failures are not silently reclassified as criteria config faults.
- [ ] DET behavior is unchanged: the config-fault verdict carries the same deterministic findings/counts as the existing degraded path, and a deterministic blocker remains BLOCK rather than being masked by INDETERMINATE.
- [ ] Focused regression tests, relevant workflow/plan-review tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass.
- [ ] The change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and no unresolved comments.
